summary: Core analysis runs on the phone (PWA, LiteRT.js) with server/phone parity; validated only on public data and in desktop Chromium. Behavioral validity, real-phone execution and production deployment are open.

behavioral_model_validity.evidence: public-data evaluations E1, E4, E7, E9-E13; semi-synthetic E8; synthetic E5
blocking: vocal-context datasets blocked by network policy (zenodo.org, huggingface.co)

on_device_compatibility_and_performance.evidence: desktop headless Chromium only (device check passes; budgets measured there)
blocking: physical tier-B phones (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) and testers (docs/DEVICE_TEST_PROTOCOL.md)

complete_product_readiness.evidence: image builds in CI; compose stack with bundle service tested locally; runbook and configuration docs
blocking: release-profile decision and legal sign-off for assets marked requires_legal_review
commercial profile: legal sign-off for every model (browser-compatible licence-confirmed detector available since E14)

multimodal_hypotheses.validation: none on real data (E5 synthetic checks)

decisions: Default phone bundle uses float32 builds; int8 bundle (14.8 MB) is an evaluated opt-in because per-image verifier decisions diverge (E12).
Dog keypoints and MammalNet-trained heads stay research-only (data terms).
Server analysis is opt-in; the default path never uploads media.
Commercial bundles must use efficientdet_lite0_tfhub_rawdecode_v1 (E14) once legal sign-off is recorded.
resources_needed: Physical phones (tier B iOS and Android at minimum) for the offline acceptance protocol
Real paired household recordings with consent and annotation (plan in docs/EVALUATION_PLAN_REAL_PAIRED.md)
Network access to zenodo.org and huggingface.co (CatMeows, Barkopedia)
Licensed cat and dog keypoint / facial / video-action datasets
GPU compute for jobs G1-G5 (docs/TRAINING_PROGRAM.md) once data exists
Hosting, domain, DNS and TLS for deployment
Legal review of model weights and training-data terms per release profile
